creativeDirection: Location photography in a cramped rehearsal room, using one plausible interior and editorial realism to stage the strongest cast inside a sleeve-derived place.
scene: A cramped, worn rehearsal basement with a cable-strewn floor, amplifiers and drum hardware pushed against the walls, and a softly glowing curtained window at one side. Four men stand close together in the near ground, thrusting their fists toward the camera as if confronting it, their faces clearly lit by the room’s practical bulbs and window spill. The room feels used and airless but readable, with a few strange, memorable objects embedded naturally in the space.

elements.element: the four men from reference image 1 posed closely together with fists extended toward the camera
the small rehearsal-room interior with worn floor, loose cables, amplifiers, and drum stands
a large window with sheer curtains glowing softly at the side of the room
a round drum painted red with small star marks resting on a low railing-like shelf
a single oversized yellow flower head lying on a case, its center ringed with multicolored sprinkled candy balls
a narrow strip of tiny red-and-blue contact-print-like photo panels taped along the base of an amplifier with no visible people in them

prompt: A cramped basement rehearsal room photographed from eye level in a tight three-quarter-length group portrait, with a worn floor scattered with cables, amplifiers and drum hardware against the walls, and a softly glowing curtained window at one side. The four men from reference image 1 are the primary subject, standing very close together in the near ground and thrusting their fists toward the camera, keeping their original front-facing pose, expression, gaze, hair, and styling, their faces clearly visible and properly lit. Build the place from reference image 2 as the main interior: scuffed floor, cable clutter, small-venue rehearsal-room density, stacked amps and stands. Add the large sheer-curtained glowing window from reference image 4 at the side of the room. Include as small supporting details a round drum painted red with tiny star marks resting on a low railing-like shelf from reference image 5, and a single oversized yellow flower head on a case with its center ringed by multicolored sprinkled candy balls from reference image 3. Add a narrow strip of tiny red-and-blue contact-print-like abstract panels taped along the base of one amplifier as a nod to reference image 7, with no people visible in those panels. Clean, crisp editorial location photography, physically plausible and cohesive, not collage. Light with bare practical bulbs in the room plus soft daytime spill through the curtained window, enough contrast to feel moody but with every cast face clean and readable. Palette of brown, beige, black, red, yellow, and cream; tense, intimate, scrappy atmosphere. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 shows four men posing closely with fists extended toward the camera, and reference image 9 is an enlarged close-up of those same people - take their faces from reference image 9. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
